title: Cohort Spec
description: The MACHINE-EXECUTABLE half of a pre-registration. The prereg's prose says what the population and exposure are for a human reader; this says it in a form pipeline/analysis/build_extract.py can execute without judgement. Both are hash-locked into the prereg, because the person who builds the analysis extract is choosing inclusion criteria — and if they do it after unlock, they are choosing them with outcomes in view. That is a p-hacking surface the gate would otherwise leave wide open.

population.description: Inclusion filters, applied in order. Every patient not matching ALL of them is excluded before any outcome is attached.

alteration_types.description: Which alteration_type values count as exposed. Listing them explicitly is the point: 'STK11 mutant' is not a definition.

oncogenic_annotation_in.description: Restrict to these oncogenic_annotation values, e.g. ['oncogenic','likely_oncogenic'] to exclude VUS.

comparator_is_complement.description: If true the comparator is everyone in the population who is not exposed. If false, `comparator` must define it explicitly — 'everyone else' is a confounder generator when the complement is heterogeneous.

modifier.description: The pre-registered effect modifier, for an interaction estimand. Its column name must match the prereg's interaction_with.

continuous.description: Keep the raw value rather than dichotomising. Where a continuous specification is better powered, dichotomising after the fact is a researcher degree of freedom — fix it here.

covariates.description: The fixed, complete covariate list. Must match the prereg's numbered list exactly; build_extract.py refuses if it does not.

name.description: Column name in the extract, matching the prereg's covariate wording.

aggregate.description: How to collapse a repeated-measures table to one row per patient. 'baseline' uses the is_baseline flag.

origin.description: Where follow-up starts. Must match the endpoint's time_origin.

left_truncate_at_sequencing.description: Enter the risk set at days_dx_to_sequencing rather than at the time origin. Required for a genomic exposure: patients must survive to be sequenced, and ignoring it manufactures a survival advantage out of ascertainment.
